suggested_fix_evaluation.coverage_caveat: funding rows exist for 12,164/12,164 wallets inside tier-A components >=5 but only 301/6,635 wallets outside any component; the honest 'main wallet -> second wallet' class the design guards against is therefore ~95% invisible to any FP simulation. Numbers below are lower bounds on FP.
suggested_fix_evaluation.assessment: The claim's fix as stated (promote peel to tier-A when funder is a contributor with first deposit within +-10%) recovers all 384 ring wallets (+303) but ALSO adds 242 non-ring wallets across 29 other clusters, including 37 ENS-named and 71 nonce>=20 wallets, mostly depth-1 'one wallet funds a few' stars (e.g. size-18 0.05-ETH cluster with 11 aged wallets, size-9 1.05-ETH cluster with zuruyu.eth/rethurd.eth) and 96 more members into the mixed 0.05-minimum mega-cluster. That is the design's named FP class and violates test_a_main_wallet_funder_outside_the_component_is_not_evidence. '~zero FP risk' is NOT supported. A chain-depth gate (funding path length >=5 hops, which a human main wallet never produces) keeps the full ring recovery and adds only ~30 non-ring wallets (3 ENS, 10 aged; 17 of them into the existing 0.05 mega-cluster). The alternative '+-5% amount union of windows' was not simulated; it would merge the entire 95.2-100.1 band (adjacent 0.1 steps are within 5%) but also the 1.19/1.29/1.39/1.49/1.59/1.69 CEX-hub staggered clusters -- risky, unevaluated.

strongest_supported_claim: One operator relayed a single ~100 ETH pot serially through ~390 wallets in hours 16-19 (origin 0x1c85cc7a, exchange-funded; terminus pays the origin back; 51 wallets swept to one collector in one block; 170 wallets share a byte-identical mint-farm history). Every hop is a funder->funded pair (380/384 resolved), but funding.py:89-90 only books a peel edge when both sit in the same tier-A component, and the operator's 0.1-ETH amount jitter puts each hop in a different single-window component (53/54 components are one window; 370/380 links discarded). Result: 303/384 wallets (79%) and 11.3% of all game points are unflagged; the 81 flagged owe it to one lucky same-window pair each. The recall gap is real and structural. The proposed fix must be depth-gated (or otherwise chain-shaped) -- the depth-agnostic +-10% version adds >=242 non-ring wallets on the available data and is untestable for the 6,334 wallets without funding rows.
